limitations: Release/default Windows FP controls. Debug, unmasked exceptions, allocation failure and arbitrary host concurrency remain unclosed.

Safe Rust owns planned reads, alias-sensitive pixel/row/plane execution and written bytes for host surface blits, copies, external alpha inversion and solid fills. Three unsafe copy sites; no assembly or new shared registry.
Native host storage must lend initialized initial-read ranges and writable output ranges in original allocations. Pointer provenance is retained; host storage is never converted to a Rust reference.
Direct cases cover exact, forward, backward and cross-row aliases in initialized bounded buffers. An FFI ownership test separately covers initially uninitialized write-then-read copy destinations.
Negative memcpy counts, overflowing geometry, metadata aliases, invalid backing storage, unknown initial-read bytes, allocation failure and arbitrary concurrency remain unresolved.
Whole-frame and creator state, color conversion, caches, host adapters and vendors remain in scope. Experimental switches remain opt-in.
COM checks use fresh disconnected objects and private volatile HKCU keys without DLL registration. Graph playback, media negotiation, UI and all host applications remain unclosed.
